newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma throws out government spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma throws out government spending cuts.

text.p: The Russian parliament's lower house rejected on Tuesday a bill scrapping scores of social benefits which the government says have grown out of proportion and became too heavy a burden for the overstretched national budget.
The communist-dominated State Duma, by 231 votes to 80, turned down the draft law presented by the cabinet, which is looking for ways to narrow a huge budget gap.

The government says that more than 100 million Russians, two-thirds of the population, receive various social benefits including tax breaks and subsidies on rent and other housing costs amounting to 350 trillion roubles ($60 billion) a year.
Government experts have said that such a situation made it practically impossible for the cabinet to meet its obligations in tight budgetary circumstances.
The government, which is seeking to cut spending under the 1997 budget to bring it into line with tax revenues that turned out to be much lower then expected.
Ministers believe that by scrapping some social benefits they could save 30 trillion roubles ($5.2 billion).
